claimed_invariant: The decimal-literal ratchet is an inventory, not a parity threshold. Updating it is legitimate only when every net increase is either a Java-cited production value or a non-shipping test expectation with a checked-in derivation, every decrease is locked, and no renderer behavior changes in the baseline commit.
causal_divergence: The baseline still records counts at 49388ae2. Later independently reviewed font, alpha, state-label, class-header, and perturbation tests added high-precision expected values, two Java-derived class constants retained more source precision, and sequence cleanup removed more literals than it added. The guard correctly reports seven per-file count changes even though the current source already contains provenance comments and the pending change needs only to ratchet the computed inventory.
planned_model_change: Regenerate decimal_literal_baseline.txt from the existing guard without changing rustuml-render or the counting algorithm. Review the exact 49388ae2-to-current literal multiset, classify production versus cfg(test) occurrences, verify adjacent Java or extraction provenance, and lock the sequence decrease. Add no allow-list, exception, threshold, or file exclusion.
perturbation_axes: net literal growth versus net literal decrease
shipping production constants versus cfg(test) expected values
Java source citation versus checked-in metrics-table derivation
count regeneration versus guard or scanner weakening
acceptance: An independent checker audits every per-file delta from baseline commit 49388ae2 to the implementation revision and records its provenance classification.
The implementation changes only decimal_literal_baseline.txt to the guard-computed counts.
Permanent hostile checks confirm an added unaccounted literal and a removed literal both make the bidirectional ratchet fail.
decimal_literal_ratchet and the complete harness_guards suite pass after the separately pending review migrations land.
scope_boundary: This mechanism changes only the frozen decimal inventory. It does not change renderer code, comparator behavior, no-oracle baselines, evidence schemas, park lists, syntax-error controls, or allow-lists.
forbidden_approaches: excluding tests or files from the scanner to reduce counts
weakening the three-decimal signature or making the ratchet one-directional
approving unexplained production constants because the aggregate count happens to balance
changing renderer output or any parity baseline in the inventory update
